subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: Should Windows exec guarantee literal `$...` PowerShell payload fidelity, or should expansion-bearing commands be handled as explicit one-shot approval/documented-limitation cases?
rationale: The current code rejects `$...` during Windows shell approval analysis, and the open PR chooses a security-boundary behavior that needs maintainer intent plus live proof before it becomes the product contract.

options.title: Adopt One-Shot Approval After Proof
options.body: Use the open PR direction, require redacted Windows/Gateway proof, and keep reusable/auto approval unavailable for expansion-bearing commands.

options.title: Guarantee Literal Forwarding
options.body: Require a runtime fix that passes `$...` payloads through unchanged while preserving approval safety for gateway and node hosts.

options.title: Document Unsupported Patterns
options.body: Treat direct `$...` PowerShell payloads as outside the guaranteed exec contract and document script-file or environment-variable workarounds.

recommendation.title: Adopt One-Shot Approval After Proof
recommendation.body: Use the open PR direction, require redacted Windows/Gateway proof, and keep reusable/auto approval unavailable for expansion-bearing commands.

likelyOwner.reason: This is now a product/security-boundary choice on core exec behavior, and Peter is the strongest available routing candidate from recent current-main history.
